text:
alex: quick Q — can we run a small latency probe against the adaptive-window cb config? want a quick sanity check before I merge the change.

maria: yes, can do. what's the target workload? short bursts or steady stream?

alex: short bursts with occasional 1k-token tails. aim is to capture p50/p95/p99 and tokens/sec. 1000 queries with variable lengths if possible.

ryan: I can run a local loadgen. use this command for reference:
```bash
python tools/loadgen.py --model rwd-adapt-v2 --concurrency 8 --iters 1000 --length-dist mix --max-tokens 1024 --out run.json
```
set `--concurrency` to 4 if you want to be conservative.

lee: heads-up: if you provoke small-batch fallback we should record the batch size distribution. also set queue_window_ms=8 for the probe so we observe the adaptive handoff.

maria: adding to that — include a warmup of ~200 iters and run with `--kv-cache=enabled`. otherwise cold-start noise will dominate p50.

alex: tagging @ryan for code review on the adaptive-window change too — PR 4821. can you cross-check perf diffs after the run? :pray:

ryan: on it. i'll run the probe now and post a quick summary. calling infra-bot to schedule a quiet window.

infra-bot: scheduled maintenance window: eng-runtime smoke-probes 2169993000–2169994200.

ryan: run complete. quick results (local dev box, A100 40GB):
- samples: 1000 (200 warmup)
- p50 latency: 12 ms
- p95 latency: 68 ms
- p99 latency: 210 ms
- tokens/sec: 23,400
- batch size distribution: median 3, 90th 8, max 16
- noted ~2% small-batch fallbacks when tail tokens >800

maria: thanks. can you dump the raw `run.json` somewhere? want to plot token-aligned latencies.

ryan: uploaded to //artifacts/eng-runtime/cb-probes/2169991234-run.json and annotated in PR 4821 comments.

lee: quick thought — try `queue_window_ms=12` next to see if p99 improves without hurting tokens/sec too much. we can compare via same loadgen.

alex: sounds good. i'll update the PR with maria/lee notes and won't merge until we validate the 12ms run. thanks for the quick turnaround :thumbsup:
